messages:
julia_sales: quick sync - Prospect (NordCredit) wants an EU-only POC. Requirements: BYOK, guaranteed EU egress (no fallback to non-EU), list of all subprocessors involved, and a rough delta vs our standard multi-region pricing. can we do this for a 30-day eval?
sam_se: Short answer: yes, but two paths: 1) tenant-pin + reserved EU capacity (recommended) or 2) deny-failover on shared infra (higher risk of 503s). We should push reserved for customer SLA needs.
marta_ops: Ops constraints: deny-failover is doable as a config flag for the POC. Behavior = requests will 503 when EU capacity exhausted. We'll emit header X-RW-Failover: denied so customer tests can detect. Also need allowlist of our EU egress IPs and certs for mutual TLS if they want network-level restrictions.
dave_fin: For cost delta, need their expected QPS / token mix. ballpark: reserved pool sized for 10M tokens/mo ~ +20-40% depending on model family and utilization. If they use large context models or low utilization we skew higher.
julia_sales: they provided numbers: 8M tokens/mo, mostly gen for chat (mix of short + occasional long). can you do a sample calc?
dave_fin: i'll model both options: tenant-pin reserved (monthly commit) and shared deny-failover (no commit, but potential request loss). will post numbers in a spreadsheet.
anna_legal: Subprocessors: compute (AWS eu-west-1), object storage (S3 eu-west-1), cdn (Fastly EU), metrics (Datadog EU), secrets (AWS KMS EU). Note: some vendors have control-plane endpoints outside EU for support telemetry - need to flag. We'll run a subproc attestation for EU-only flow and propose DPA amendment for POC.
sam_se: BYOK notes: we support AWS KMS customer keys in-region for Hosted POCs (with limited support). For Dedicated/Private we can accept on-prem HSM but that is a different contract. For BYOK handshake: customer must grant our service principal Encrypt/Decrypt and we run a test envelope exchange.
marta_ops: ops checklist draft:
```
- Create tenant_pin config (eu-west-1)
- Set routing.failover_policy = deny-failover
- Provision reserved pool (if requested)
- Register BYOK key ARN in onboarding portal
- Add customer IP ranges to egress allowlist
- Run subproc attestation and share PDF
- Schedule 1hr DR test window (simulate saturation)
```

julia_sales: customer wants the official subprocessors list and a short note on what "deny-failover" means for their app (they'll give this to security/compliance). can legal + ops produce something short to share?
anna_legal: yes. i'll produce a 1-page memo: list, residual risks, and proposed DPA clause language. ETA 36h.
dave_fin: i'll attach two cost scenarios in the spreadsheet today: (A) reserved 8M tokens baseline, (B) shared deny-failover with no reservation. include estimated SLA risk premium for reserved option.
sam_se: Testing guidance for customer: do a steady ramp to saturate EU pool and assert that you see 503 + X-RW-Failover: denied in response headers. sample curl:
```
curl -H "x-tenant: nordcredit" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":512}' -i
```
look for 503 status and header. We'll also give them a small harness to replay recorded traffic.
marta_ops: note: telemetry - application-level logs and metrics can be sent to Datadog EU, but our infra agent currently sends some health checks to a global control plane (no PII). we'll list those endpoints in the attestation.
infra-bot: infra-bot: reserved-pool request created: RP-1797554321 (eu-west-1)
julia_sales: action items summary: sam -> SE doc + test harness, marta -> ops checklist + allowed IPs, dave -> cost spreadsheet, anna -> subproc memo + DPA snippet. i'll consolidate and share with NordCredit. :thumbsup:
sam_se: will add a short FAQ about fail modes and mitigation (retry, exponential backoff, local caching).
julia_sales: thanks team. ping me when docs are ready so i can move the deal forward. :rocket:
